findings.note: Misleading comment claiming coverage that does not exist: the comment says 'escalation over three failed forks of the parent lineage is refused with the human-only code', but the assertion beneath it is h.mustErr("ERR_CHECKPOINT_NOT_FOUND", 2, "advance", "--run", id, "--from", "nope"), which exercises an unknown checkpoint name, not escalation. ERR_RUN_ESCALATED (machine/fork.go:82) is never driven through the CLI in this file; it is only covered at the machine layer (internal/fsm/machine/fork_test.go:600). The CLI-level contract documented in prompt.go:38 and CLAUDE.md (escalation refuses with exit 2 and waits for a human) is therefore asserted nowhere end to end. Behaviour is correct by inspection (the code lands in the exit2 map in envelope.go:55), so this is a comment/coverage-claim defect, not a functional one.

findings.note: The panic assertion tests less than its failure message claims. t.Fatal("rand failure panics into ERR_INTERNAL") implies a crypto/rand failure surfaces as the ERR_INTERNAL JSON envelope, but the test calls (&ctxDeps{deps: h.deps}).nonce() directly and only asserts that a panic occurs. A grep for recover() across the CLI package finds exactly one hit and it is this test: wiring.go:170 is the only panic site in internal/fsm/cli, internal/fsm/machine and internal/fsm/run, and nothing recovers it, so in the real binary a crypto/rand failure aborts with a Go stack trace instead of the single-JSON-object stdout plus exit code every other path guarantees to the agent driver. Practically unreachable (crypto/rand does not fail on the supported platforms), so it is worth a comment fix or a recover in Run rather than blocking.

evidence.note: message asserts ERR_INTERNAL while the test only observes a raw panic from nonce()
the sole panic site in the CLI/machine/run packages, with no recover anywhere in the package

findings.note: Two harness assertions can panic instead of failing cleanly, which would turn a future regression into an index-out-of-range crash rather than a readable test failure. h.run indexes args[0] when the stdout envelope fails to unmarshal, and h.run() is called with zero args from TestUsageAndPrompt (h.mustErr(CodeUsage, 2)); today the empty-args path does emit JSON so the short-circuit saves it, but the guard is one regression away from panicking. Likewise the agent-prompt assertion slices h.out.String()[:80] on the failure branch, which panics whenever the failing output is shorter than 80 bytes — exactly the case where the prompt was not written.

evidence.note: args[0] is read when unmarshal fails, and h.run() is legitimately called with no args
h.out.String()[:80] panics on short output in the failure path
